items.title: GTA 6's Cool Dog will rescue you on a jet ski
items.note: Get stranded at sea in GTA 6 and a dog on a jet ski shows up to save you, and the internet is in love.
items.read: Dexerto reports that if you get stranded in the ocean in GTA 6, a dog driving a jet ski comes to rescue you. Cool Dog then takes you to an island full of other dogs where you can play fetch and dig up $1,218. A follow-up Dexerto post says the character is based on a real dog named Loosy, who skis and hoverboards with her owner around Fort Lauderdale.

items.title: The GTA 6 furry side quest pays $15,000
items.note: GTA 6's world bans furries, but players found you can help one instead, and it pays.
items.read: According to Dexerto, furries are 'illegal' in GTA 6's satirical world, but players can choose to help one. A furry called Chase offers either $15,000 in cash or a custom SMG in exchange for your help. It's classic Rockstar parody, and the post racked up huge numbers on launch day.

items.title: 'The most disrespectful thing in Mario Party history'
items.note: A 22-second Mario Party clip that people are calling peak game-night betrayal.
items.read: Massimo (@Rainmaker1973) shared a short Mario Party clip with the caption 'The most disrespectful thing in Mario Party history has just happened.' The post gives no other details, so watch it to see the betrayal for yourself. It's the kind of moment that ends friendships on game night.

items.title: Just Eat made a controller with a 'ChEAT' button
items.note: A dedicated button that orders food so you never have to pause the game, timed for GTA 6 week.
items.read: Just Eat has made a gaming controller with a button for ordering food. Pressing the 'ChEAT' button triggers a delivery. The device is only available through a UK giveaway, so for most of us it stays a very relatable fantasy.

items.title: Jokić on GTA 6: 'I play League of Legends on the phone'
items.note: The whole world is playing GTA 6, and the NBA superstar just shrugs it off.
items.read: Nikola Jokić was asked whether he's going to play GTA 6. His answer: 'No … I play League of Legends on the phone.' A perfectly deadpan answer on GTA's biggest launch day.

items.title: WhatsApp briefly became 'WhatUp!' for GTA 6
items.note: A real app rebranding itself as its own in-game parody is peak launch-week energy.
items.read: Dexerto reports that WhatsApp temporarily rebranded to 'WhatUp!' for the GTA 6 release. WhatUp! is the game's in-world parody of the app, so the real brand joined in on the joke.

items.title: Burger King's adult Snoopy meal comes with a beanie
items.note: A Happy Meal for grown-ups, in a doghouse box, and people are very into it.
items.read: Burger King is releasing adult Snoopy meals in the US with collectible beanies. They come in a Snoopy Doghouse Box with a choice of Whopper or Chicken Nuggets, loaded potato tots and a new Cookies & Creme Pie. The post drew over 500 quote posts.

items.title: Peekaboo 😅
items.note: A 3-second 'peekaboo' clip from Buitengebieden, the feel-good animal account, short enough to replay forever.
items.read: Buitengebieden, an account known for wholesome nature and animal clips, posted a 3-second video captioned simply 'Peekaboo.. 😅'. The post doesn't say more than that. It's a quick, light watch.

items.title: Men's Day shares a date with World Toilet Day 😂
items.note: As #اليوم_العالمي_للرجل trended in Saudi Arabia, a Gulf user pointed out that International Men's Day shares Nov 19 with World Toilet Day.

This post points out, in Gulf Arabic, that it falls on the same date as World Toilet Day: 'so don't get too excited' 😂. A small post, but it sums up the mood of the hashtag.

items.title: SASSO, VIA Riyadh
items.note: Doha's award-winning Italian spot just opened its first Saudi branch, mid-Riyadh Season.
items.read: SASSO, known in Doha for tagliatelle tossed inside an aged Parmesan wheel and its Wagyu Pinwheel Lasagna, is now open at VIA Riyadh in Al Hada. Its Al Hazm branch won Favourite Italian Fine Dining at the FACT Dining Awards Doha 2022. Booking ahead is advised, especially on weekends.

article.html:
SASSO, the Doha Italian restaurant known for its Parmesan-wheel tagliatelle and Wagyu lasagna, has opened its first Saudi branch at VIA Riyadh, open daily from 5pm to 1am.

8NovemberVIA Riyadh, Al Hada, Riyadh

VIA Riyadh, Makkah Al Mukarramah Road, Al Hada, Riyadh

Location

SASSO, the Italian restaurant that made its name in Doha, has opened at VIA Riyadh. It is the brand's first branch in Saudi Arabia, and it arrives in the middle of Riyadh Season, when VIA Riyadh is one of the busiest dining addresses in the city.

The restaurant comes with a strong reputation at home. Its Al Hazm branch in Doha won Favourite Italian Fine Dining at the FACT Dining Awards Doha 2022, and the brand also runs restaurants at West Walk and Place Vendôme in the Qatari capital. When the move to Riyadh was announced in October, no opening date was given; the restaurant is now taking guests.

The Riyadh menu leans on the dishes SASSO is known for. There is Pasta Al Forno, baked fusilli with organic chicken, mushrooms and Parmesan in a creamy pink sauce, and a Wagyu Pinwheel Lasagna, rolled pasta filled with Wagyu bolognese and beef bacon. The table-side dish is the tagliatelle, tossed inside a large aged Parmesan wheel in front of you. Other plates include spicy rigatoni with burrata, a wood-fired black truffle pizza, chicken Milanese and a veal risotto topped with veal that is slow-cooked for six hours.

SASSO joins a strip of well-known international names at VIA Riyadh, the open-air dining and shopping district on Makkah Al Mukarramah Road in Al Hada, which is also home to The St. Regis Riyadh. Gymkhana, Madeo and Berenjak already serve there, and the Qatari café NOIR opened its second Riyadh branch in the same district last month. Riyadh Season began on 21 October and runs for about ten weeks, so the evenings around VIA Riyadh are at their fullest right now.

SASSO opens every day from 5pm to 1am. Booking ahead is advised, especially at the weekend, and the dress code is smart casual or business casual. Prices have not been published yet, and no online booking page has been announced, so for now a table is booked by contacting the restaurant directly.

article.html:
The Qatari café and restaurant NOIR now has a second home in Riyadh, at entrance V8 of VIA Riyadh in Al Hada, open daily from 4pm to midnight.

10NovemberVIA Riyadh, Al Hada, Riyadh

NOIR, the café and restaurant brand from Qatar, has opened its second branch in Riyadh, at VIA Riyadh in Al Hada. The café's own website now lists the new address, entrance V8 of VIA Riyadh, next to its first Riyadh branch in Laysen Valley on King Khalid Road.

The new branch keeps the look the brand is known for: a dark, glossy front under hanging plants and strings of warm lights, crystal chandeliers inside, a black and white chequered floor, and a terrace with sofas facing the walkway. Platinumlist's guide, which reported the opening, says it opens daily from 4pm to midnight and recommends booking a table.

The dine-in menu mixes European and Asian dishes. NOIR lists truffle and mushroom soup and tom yum among its soups; burrata, beetroot, Wagyu Thai and little gem Caesar salads; a golden truffle pizza, a margherita and its own "NOIR Pizza Arabica Roll"; a mushroom and truffle risotto; Wagyu striploin, ribeye and Wagyu stroganoff steaks; and dishes such as Andhra chicken biryani, grilled salmon and shrimp linguine. The café also has separate breakfast, sweets and coffee menus, and the guide singles out its tiramisu and chocolate fondant.

NOIR first came to Riyadh in 2025, when it opened in Laysen Valley. VIA Riyadh, the open-air shopping and dining quarter in Al Hada, has been adding names this season: SASSO, the Italian restaurant from Doha, opened there earlier this month, alongside restaurants such as Gymkhana and Madeo.

The café has not published prices on its website, and the menu online does not list them, so expect them at the table. NOIR does not say whether walk-ins are taken at the busiest hours.

For a table, call the café on +966 11 511 5747 (the number its website gives for both Riyadh branches) or message its Instagram account, @cafenoir.ksa. The branch is at entrance V8 of VIA Riyadh, Al Hada, and opens every day from 4pm to midnight. The first branch in Laysen Valley stays open, so check which one you are booking.

items.title: Le Café NAC, Aseel Resort Diriyah
items.note: London's Belgravia café brought a winter outdoor pop-up to Wadi Hanifah.
items.read: Le Café NAC opened a winter pop-up at Aseel Resort in Diriyah on November 5, with bistro seating, greenery and warm lighting for the cooler evenings. In London it's known for breakfast burritos, ricotta pancakes and black truffle rigatoni, though the Diriyah menu hasn't been fully revealed. Reservations go through The Chefz.

article.html:
Looking for somewhere new to enjoy the cooler weather in Riyadh? Le Café NAC has brought its London café concept to Diriyah, opening a winter pop-up at Aseel Resort.

The restaurant officially opened on November 5, bringing its French-inspired brasserie style to an outdoor setting with bistro-style seating, greenery, warm lighting and a relaxed atmosphere. It’s a new spot to consider for dinner, coffee or an evening catch-up with friends.

What To Expect At Le Café NAC

Originally from London’s Belgravia neighbourhood, Le Café NAC is known for its relaxed café atmosphere and menu of comfort food with a contemporary twist.

Its London menu features favourites such as breakfast burritos, tuna melts, ricotta pancakes, burgers and black truffle rigatoni. One of its popular desserts is crushed milk chocolate cookies served with soft serve and crispy cereal.

The full menu for the Diriyah pop-up has not yet been revealed, so it’s not confirmed which of these dishes will be available at Aseel Resort.

Where Can You Find It?

Le Café NAC’s winter pop-up is located at Aseel Resort in Wadi Hanifah, Diriyah. The outdoor space features intimate tables, greenery and warm lighting, making it a setting for an evening out during Riyadh’s cooler months.

The pop-up is open daily from 6pm to midnight, and reservations are available through The Chefz. A booking fee of SAR50 per person applies.

Le Café NAC at Aseel Resort

  • Location: Aseel Resort, Wadi Hanifah, Diriyah
  • Opening hours: Daily, 6pm to midnight
  • Reservations: Book through The Chefz
  • Booking fee: SAR50 per person

The winter residency is now open, although an official closing date has not yet been announced.

article.html:
Grand Hyatt The Red Sea Officially Opens On Shura Island, Establishing A New Hub For Exceptional Stays, Dining And Events

The 430-room resort combines elevated stays, grand-scale events and a vibrant culinary and lifestyle offering

CHICAGO (November 2, 2026): Hyatt Hotels Corporation (NYSE: H) announces the opening of Grand Hyatt The Red Sea on Shura Island, marking the arrival of the second Hyatt branded property in The Red Sea coastal destination and the eighth Hyatt branded hotel in The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Positioned as a destination within a destination, Grand Hyatt The Red Sea combines elevated stays, grand-scale events, and a lively culinary and lifestyle offering, alongside family-friendly activities, adults-only spaces and wellness facilities catering to every style of stay. The property is set to become the heart of Shura Island, as well as a leading venue for meetings, celebrations and landmark gatherings.

“The opening of Grand Hyatt The Red Sea is a significant milestone for Hyatt in the Kingdom and comes just months after Miraval The Red Sea welcomed guests earlier this year,” said Stephen Ansell, Managing Director, Middle East and Africa, Hyatt. “Together, these openings reflect our pace and ambition for growing our brands in Saudi Arabia, while giving World of Hyatt members even more ways to experience this extraordinary destination across two distinctive Hyatt brands. We are proud to be playing a role in bringing Shura Island’s vision to life.”

Grand Hyatt The Red Sea offers 430 rooms, suites and villas, the island’s leading ballroom and nine distinctive dining venues, making it the island’s largest gathering and dining destinations.

Guided by Shura Island’s regenerative Coral Bloom master planning concept created by Foster + Partners, Grand Hyatt The Red Sea’s design draws directly from its setting. Inspired by the colours, textures and organic forms of the Red Sea’s coral reefs, the resort’s signature canopy structures create a distinctive visual identity while providing shade and comfortable outdoor spaces that encourage exploration and social interaction. Made using recycled fishing nets and inspired by reef forms, prisms of light and reflections on the water, the canopies form part of a wider design approach that connects the resort to its natural surroundings while supporting the destination’s environmental ambitions.

“It is an honor to welcome guests to Grand Hyatt The Red Sea,” said Jean-Francois Durand, General Manager at Grand Hyatt The Red Sea. “Shura Island is unlike anywhere else, and we've designed every part of the experience, from our rooms and pools to our nine dining venues, to reflect the vibrancy and beauty of this incredible destination. We can't wait to share it with the rest of the world.”

Spacious Accommodation

Grand Hyatt The Red Sea features 430 rooms, suites and villas, designed to offer spacious and comfortable retreats with a strong connection to the surrounding landscape. Designed by Muza Lab, the accommodations draw on the Coral Bloom concept, The Reef Flower Garden, with a calming palette, soft warmth and organic forms inspired by the Red Sea. Layered textures and playful accents echo the movement of the ocean and its changing tides, creating interiors that feel both serene and intrinsically connected to their surroundings. Guest rooms feature private balconies or terraces overlooking the sea, lagoon or gardens, alongside premium bedding, spa-inspired bathrooms, high-speed Wi-Fi, smart in-room technology, luxury bath amenities and curated minibars. Select accommodations also feature private pools and exclusive villa experiences, offering guests an elevated level of comfort and privacy while connecting them to the natural beauty of The Red Sea.

Vibrant Culinary Offering

The expansive resort will be home to nine distinctive dining and social venues, creating a diverse culinary destination for guests and visitors to Shura Island, with experiences ranging from live-fire dining and international cuisine to relaxed poolside venues and late-night social concepts.

Now open, guests can gather at Embers, where the spectacle of live-fire cooking takes center stage, showcasing expertly prepared meats and fresh seafood in a vibrant setting inspired by the spirit of shared dining. For a more relaxed experience, Drift Pool Bar will offer refreshing beverages and light bites alongside sweeping views of The Red Sea, creating an inviting setting to unwind throughout the day.

The resort's culinary offering will continue to evolve, with the seven other venues set to open at a later stage. items.note: London's huge new free museum opens in the restored Victorian General Market on Nov 28.
items.read: London Museum is opening new free permanent galleries in Smithfield's General Market, finishing a decade-long restoration of the Victorian building. It will tell the city's story with iconic and never-before-seen objects, plus a day-to-night events programme; the first, London Tastes, is co-curated by Ruby Tandoh and Jonathan Nunn.

article.html:
A visualisation of London Museum’s Past Time galleries © Secchi Smith Atelier Brückner.

  • London Museum’s new free permanent galleries will open in Smithfield on 28 November 2026.
  • A major new cultural destination, the museum brings together thousands of years of London’s history alongside a new social space for the city.
  • A day to night programme of events, experiences and entertainment will be shaped by rotating Guest Editors. The inaugural programme – London Tastes – will be co-curated by Ruby Tandoh and Jonathan Nunn and sponsored by Sainsbury’s.
  • Over 100,000 people have contributed to the creation of the new museum, which will tell the story of one of the world’s greatest cities in all its grit and glitter, showcasing iconic objects and never-before-seen items.
  • Reopening in time for the museum’s 50th anniversary, the launch marks the culmination of a decade-long transformation of Smithfield’s historic General Market. The adjacent Poultry Market will open in 2028, expanding the museum with two temporary exhibition spaces, a dedicated learning centre and a collections store.

18 June, London: London Museum has today announced it will open the doors to its new permanent galleries in Smithfield’s General Market on 28 November 2026, marking a new chapter for the world’s largest city museum. At its heart, London Museum has been envisioned as a social space for the city, drawing on the distinctive architecture of the market to unite the museum’s collection and London’s communities, to honour the past and present of this major global capital.

Designed by Stanton Williams and Asif Khan, alongside conservation architects Julian Harrap, the museum is located in one of the oldest parts of the capital, the City of London. The opening completes a decade-long restoration of the Victorian General Market, returning the disused historic building to public use for the first time in over three decades. The £437m project has been developed through a unique partnership between the City of London Corporation and Mayor of London Sadiq Khan, alongside support from a range of philanthropic supporters including Bloomberg Philanthropies, the Goldsmiths’ Foundation, The Linbury Trust and The National Lottery Heritage Fund.

In the General Market, the museum unfolds across three interconnected spaces. Visitors will enter via Real Time (on Heritage Fund Street) – a covered former street that acts as the museum’s main entrance – enriched by data capturing London in the moment. From there, they move into Our Time (in the Linbury Hall), a vibrant central hub for events and activities, anchored by 13 large installations – eclectic objects from London in living memory. Below ground, in the museum’s cavernous subterranean galleries, the permanent displays of Past Time offer a compelling overview of London’s history through chronological and thematic displays.

Highlights confirmed for display across the museum include the Whitechapel Fatberg, The Lord Mayor’s Coach, Banksy’s Piranhas artwork, Charles I’s execution vest, Emmeline Pankhurst’s hunger strike medal and Anna Pavlova’s ‘Dying Swan’ dress. There will be objects from the museum’s eminent archaeological archive, including Roman writing tablets from The Bloomberg Collection capturing the city’s earliest surviving voices. The tablets form part of The Bloomberg Collection, a world-renowned trove of more than 14,000 Roman artefacts, the largest archaeological deposition ever gifted to the museum. In The Goldsmiths’ Gallery, the glittering Cheapside Hoard, one of the most significant collections of Elizabethan and Jacobean jewellery, will be shown in the fullest display of the hoard ever assembled. A more detailed overview of London Museum’s highlight objects is available HERE.

Sharon Ament, Director, London Museum said: “This has been a long undertaking – not without its challenges but mostly filled with immense joy and hyper-creativity – and now we are counting down the days to welcome our first visitors. At the beginning we asked ourselves how to be the best museum for London, the answer is, to be London itself, in all its grit and glitter. We’ve done it with the very best; designers, historians, curators, builders, architects, artists, poets, writers, creators to name a few, all are shapers of London. And the very best includes over one hundred thousand people who have contributed along the way. I hope our museum is a place where people can come together, feel at home, and find themselves grounded in the lives, treasures, challenges and innovations of this city’s vast history. Above all, I hope we make Londoners proud!”

Christopher Hayward, Policy Chairman, City of London Corporation said: “This is a landmark moment for the Square Mile and the City of London Corporation is proud to have been a major partner in making this happen and funding it.

London Museum at Smithfield is a flagship investment that brings new life to one of our most historic buildings, opening it up for the public to enjoy for the first time in a generation. This sits at the heart of our Destination City vision, a Square Mile that is alive seven days a week, where world-class culture, history and ambition exist side by side.

By combining world-class heritage with a dynamic programme of events and experiences, the museum will not only tell London’s story in all its richness, but play a vital role in shaping its future, strengthening the City’s appeal as a place to work, visit and invest.”

The Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, said: “The opening of the new London Museum will be a hugely significant moment both for London and internationally. Backed by one of the largest ever cultural investments in our capital, London Museum will attract millions of visitors and Londoners and reinforce our status as the culture capital of the world. London Museum celebrates the past, creates opportunities in the present and will inspire future generations, as we continue to build a better London for everyone.”

Our Time – in the Linbury Hall

  • Visualisation of London Museum’s Our Time space © Secchi Smith / Asif Khan.

  • Visualisation of London Museum’s Our Time space © Secchi Smith / Asif Khan.

At the heart of the museum is Our Time in the Linbury Hall, a new social space for London set beneath the market’s restored dome. Here, visitors can gather and experience London’s vibrant culture as it unfolds under one roof.

Around its perimeter, a restaurant, shop and show space for families and schools will sit alongside 13 large anchor displays. These eclectic snapshots of London in living memory will include the Lord Mayor’s Coach, paraded annually on London’s streets, and East End icon Syd’s Coffee Stall. Hanging Out – a display paying homage to places that have brought Londoners together – will include signs from the India Club, Topshop and the Galtymore Dance Club, whilst the voices of London’s Generation Alpha will be captured by a display drawn from the museum’s first major collecting project with young people.

A day to night programme of activities will animate Our Time’s centre, delivered with London partners including Morley’s chicken shop, Punchdrunk Enrichment and Hive Curates.

Highlights will include:

  • Tuesday Tea Club (every Tuesday, from November 2026) – free hot brews from Syd’s Coffee Stall. Joining the museum's collection in 2019 after 100 years of trading in Shoreditch, Syd’s will bring Londoners together over workshops, live performances and more.
  • Shared Late Nights (every Friday and Saturday, from November 2026) – The lights go down and the music goes up in these after-hours sessions, featuring curated DJ sets.
  • Dinner Club (monthly, from January 2027) – For the foodies, London's best culinary talent will serve up a monthly feast, framed by a distinct theme and served up with a side of entertainment.
  • House Party (first Saturday of the month, from February 2027) – the museum’s monthly bash – a chance to mingle amongst the artefacts and make the market floor your dance floor.

For young visitors and families:

  • Playdates (Every Saturday, from January 2027) – co-produced with leading immersive theatre company Punchdrunk Enrichment. A new experience for families will bring magic to the museum’s galleries, in pursuit of one of London’s most elusive creatures. Recommended for ages 7+.
  • Showspace (Sundays from November 2026, Sunday to Friday from February 2027) – Sensory storytelling and performance bring to life events of the Great Fire, Roman London and other hidden stories that have shaped our city in these free interactive shows for schools and families. Recommended for ages 5+.

LONDON TASTES

The museum will invite Guest Editors to explore the city through their eyes, reflecting on one of four key themes: tastes, sounds, plays and wears. Their ideas will act as a unifying thread, shaping a season of experiences and events that run through Our Time, including its regular house parties, family events and dinner clubs, as well as influencing the museum’s shop and restaurant. In a vibrant, evolving city of almost 10 million people, they will offer visitors the chance to experience a slice of their city.

The museum’s inaugural programme, London Tastes (November 2026 – August 2027) will celebrate the city’s rich and vibrant food culture, led by Guest Editors Ruby Tandoh (All Consuming, Cook As You Are), whose work explores the intersections of food and social change, and Jonathan Nunn, founder of the influential food publication Vittles. The programme is sponsored by Sainsbury’s, whose roots in London date back to its first store on Drury Lane over 150 years ago.

London Tastes will feature a spotlight exhibition across two display pavilions, exploring the changing appetites of a global food city. Crossing London’s neighbourhoods from Enfield to Park Royal, Southall to Walworth, it will touch on stories of Covent Garden market, Brick Lane, London’s traditional pie and mash shops, chicken shop culture, and the markets, manufacturers, retailers and artisans that make up London’s ever-evolving food scene.

Mark Given, Chief Technology, Marketing and Data Officer at Sainsbury's said: "Good food has always been about bringing people together across communities, cultures and generations and for more than 150 years, Sainsbury's has been part of that story. From our first store at 173 Drury Lane, helping Londoners shop, cook and gather has always been at the heart of what we do.

We're thrilled to come on board as Principal Sponsor of London Tastes – the debut creative programme at the brand-new London Museum – a programme that celebrates the rich heritage and food culture of this city, while looking ahead to the future. This partnership is a brilliant reflection of what we stand for at Sainsbury’s too – championing good food for all of us.”

Past Time

A visualisation of London Museum’s Past Time galleries © Secchi Smith Atelier Brückner.

Descending below ground into the permanent galleries set at Roman street level, visitors will encounter the stories and people that have shaped London through time – from the lives of the earliest prehistoric inhabitants and rare artefacts from the city’s Roman origins nearly 2000 years ago, to transformative events including the Great Fire and the Blitz, and cultural milestones like the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Voices of past Londoner’s will shine through in object-rich, theatrical and sensory displays, presented both chronologically and thematically for the first time.

Drawn from the museum’s 7-million-strong collection – the world’s largest relating to a single urban centre – Past Time reveals a city shaped as much by its grit as its glitter. In its first permanent display, the Cheapside Hoard will dazzle alongside rare objects from the Goldsmiths’ Company collection. Old favourites will return including the glamorous Selfridges lift and a chunk of the infamous Whitechapel Fatberg. There will be artefacts linked to iconic Londoners and defining moments for the capital – including Tom Daley’s 2012 Olympic diving trunks, Queen Victoria’s mourning dress, Charles Dickens’ chair and the vest believed to have been worn by King Charles I at his execution (on display for six months).

London’s rich history as an epicentre of protest and activism is also explored, from an unparalleled collection of suffragette material – including Emmeline Pankhurst’s hunger strike medal and the court warrant issued to Sophia Duleep Singh – to more contemporary objects such as a statuette of Lady Phyll, co-founder of UK Black Pride, and placards from trailblazing disabled-led group Transport for All. From punk to ballet, London’s status as a global creative powerhouse will shine through iconic cultural artefacts: On loan from The Clash’s Paul Simonon, the smashed Fender Precision Bass guitar, immortalised on the band’s 1979 album London Calling, tablas belonging to British Bhangra pioneer Kuljit Bhamra and Anna Pavlova’s Dying Swan costume.

Set amongst displays exploring London's evolving landscape, a six-metre viewing window will offer visitors a world first museum experience: the chance to watch live trains rumble through the galleries as passengers peer in from the passing Thameslink line.

A visualisation of London Museum’s train window in the Past Time galleries © Secchi Smith Atelier Brückner.

Restoring the General Market

The restored General Market dome © London Museum.

Opened in 1883 and designed by Sir Horace Jones – the architect behind Tower Bridge and Leadenhall Market – the Victorian General Market saw over a century of trade before being shuttered in the 1990s and falling into disrepair. Leading its meticulous restoration and transformation are Stanton Williams and Asif Khan, working with conservation architects Julian Harrap. Together they are moulding a historic landmark into a sustainable 21st century cultural destination.

The vast project has drawn on expertise from over 70 trades, and since 2023 has given more than 40 apprentices a start in fields ranging from plumbing and electrical engineering to emerging disciplines like sustainable construction management. The building’s heritage as a working market is being carefully preserved and celebrated through the work of some of the UK’s leading craftspeople – from the country’s last heritage coppersmiths to master stonemasons and Welsh blacksmiths restoring decorative ironwork. The reanimation of these historic buildings has been guided by their distinctive character – with features including a rediscovered 800sqm system of vaults beneath London’s streets and a perimeter of heritage shopfronts. At the same time, the project will be futureproofed for generations to come as a world-leading ‘green museum’. Incorporating cutting-edge sustainability measures – from toilets powered by rainwater to renewable geothermal energy and an industry-first eco-concrete mix – it is set to rank among the top 1% of buildings worldwide with a BREEAM ‘Outstanding’ sustainability rating.

In the district of Smithfield, the museum will be embedded in an area that has been a centre for trade and exchange for almost a millennium, opposite the 900-year-old St Bartholomew’s Hospital with its elegant Hogarth Staircase, and a stone’s throw away from the internationally renowned Barbican Arts Centre and London’s majestic icon: St Paul’s Cathedral. The surrounding City of London is the capital’s most historic quarter, a former home to Shakespeare and depicted in the books of Charles Dickens, it has provided the backdrop to numerous films, TV series and music videos ranging from The Crown to Slow Horses, thanks to its iconic mix of architecture. It is home to an extraordinary 600 listed buildings, 28 conservation areas, 48 scheduled ancient monuments and four historic parks and gardens.

London Museum is London’s shared place in the middle of it all.

No matter where you’ve come from, how long you’re staying for, or what side of the river you live on, we offer a home for exploration and adventure where all of London’s stories cross and collide.

At our heart we're a social history museum and we tell the stories of how London came to be. But we're also contemporary collectors keeping our finger on the pulse. We're the world's biggest city museum.

At the core of London Museum is our collection, which covers 450,000 years of history through seven million objects drawn from across all 33 boroughs. It's the largest collection in the world relating to a single urban centre.

The City of London Corporation is one of the largest funders of heritage and cultural activities in the UK, investing over £145m every year. It manages a range of world-class cultural and heritage institutions, including the Barbican Centre, Tower Bridge, Guildhall School of Music & Drama, Guildhall Library, Guildhall Art Gallery and London’s Roman Amphitheatre, The London Archives, and Keats House. At its heart, London Museum has been envisioned as a social space for the city, drawing on the distinctive architecture of the market to unite the museum’s collection and London’s communities, to honour the past and present of this major global capital.Designed by Stanton Williams and Asif Khan, alongside conservation architects Julian Harrap, the museum is located in one of the oldest parts of the capital, the City of London. The opening completes a decade-long restoration of the Victorian General Market, returning the disused historic building to public use for the first time in over three decades. The £437m project has been developed through a unique partnership between the City of London Corporation and Mayor of London Sadiq Khan, alongside support from a range of philanthropic supporters including Bloomberg Philanthropies, the Goldsmiths’ Foundation, The Linbury Trust and The National Lottery Heritage Fund.In the General Market, the museum unfolds across three interconnected spaces. Visitors will enter via Real Time (on Heritage Fund Street) – a covered former street that acts as the museum’s main entrance – enriched by data capturing London in the moment. From there, they move into Our Time (in the Linbury Hall), a vibrant central hub for events and activities, anchored by 13 large installations – eclectic objects from London in living memory. Below ground, in the museum’s cavernous subterranean galleries, the permanent displays of Past Time offer a compelling overview of London’s history through chronological and thematic displays.Highlights confirmed for display across the museum include the Whitechapel Fatberg, The Lord Mayor’s Coach, Banksy’s Piranhas artwork, Charles I’s execution vest, Emmeline Pankhurst’s hunger strike medal and Anna Pavlova’s ‘Dying Swan’ dress. There will be objects from the museum’s eminent archaeological archive, including Roman writing tablets from The Bloomberg Collection capturing the city’s earliest surviving voices. The tablets form part of The Bloomberg Collection, a world-renowned trove of more than 14,000 Roman artefacts, the largest archaeological deposition ever gifted to the museum. In The Goldsmiths’ Gallery, the glittering Cheapside Hoard, one of the most significant collections of Elizabethan and Jacobean jewellery, will be shown in the fullest display of the hoard ever assembled. A more detailed overview of London Museum’s highlight objects is available HERE.Sharon Ament, Director, London Museum said: “This has been a long undertaking – not without its challenges but mostly filled with immense joy and hyper-creativity – and now we are counting down the days to welcome our first visitors. At the beginning we asked ourselves how to be the best museum for London, the answer is, to be London itself, in all its grit and glitter. We’ve done it with the very best; designers, historians, curators, builders, architects, artists, poets, writers, creators to name a few, all are shapers of London. And the very best includes over one hundred thousand people who have contributed along the way. I hope our museum is a place where people can come together, feel at home, and find themselves grounded in the lives, treasures, challenges and innovations of this city’s vast history. Above all, I hope we make Londoners proud!”Christopher Hayward, Policy Chairman, City of London Corporation said: “This is a landmark moment for the Square Mile and the City of London Corporation is proud to have been a major partner in making this happen and funding it.London Museum at Smithfield is a flagship investment that brings new life to one of our most historic buildings, opening it up for the public to enjoy for the first time in a generation. This sits at the heart of our Destination City vision, a Square Mile that is alive seven days a week, where world-class culture, history and ambition exist side by side.By combining world-class heritage with a dynamic programme of events and experiences, the museum will not only tell London’s story in all its richness, but play a vital role in shaping its future, strengthening the City’s appeal as a place to work, visit and invest.”The Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, said: “The opening of the new London Museum will be a hugely significant moment both for London and internationally. Backed by one of the largest ever cultural investments in our capital, London Museum will attract millions of visitors and Londoners and reinforce our status as the culture capital of the world. London Museum celebrates the past, creates opportunities in the present and will inspire future generations, as we continue to build a better London for everyone.”
Visualisation of London Museum’s Our Time space © Secchi Smith / Asif Khan.
Visualisation of London Museum’s Our Time space © Secchi Smith / Asif Khan.

At the heart of the museum is Our Time in the Linbury Hall, a new social space for London set beneath the market’s restored dome. Here, visitors can gather and experience London’s vibrant culture as it unfolds under one roof.Around its perimeter, a restaurant, shop and show space for families and schools will sit alongside 13 large anchor displays. These eclectic snapshots of London in living memory will include the Lord Mayor’s Coach, paraded annually on London’s streets, and East End icon Syd’s Coffee Stall. Hanging Out – a display paying homage to places that have brought Londoners together – will include signs from the India Club, Topshop and the Galtymore Dance Club, whilst the voices of London’s Generation Alpha will be captured by a display drawn from the museum’s first major collecting project with young people.A day to night programme of activities will animate Our Time’s centre, delivered with London partners including Morley’s chicken shop, Punchdrunk Enrichment and Hive Curates.Highlights will include:Tuesday Tea Club (every Tuesday, from November 2026) – free hot brews from Syd’s Coffee Stall. Joining the museum's collection in 2019 after 100 years of trading in Shoreditch, Syd’s will bring Londoners together over workshops, live performances and more.Shared Late Nights (every Friday and Saturday, from November 2026) – The lights go down and the music goes up in these after-hours sessions, featuring curated DJ sets.Dinner Club (monthly, from January 2027) – For the foodies, London's best culinary talent will serve up a monthly feast, framed by a distinct theme and served up with a side of entertainment.House Party (first Saturday of the month, from February 2027) – the museum’s monthly bash – a chance to mingle amongst the artefacts and make the market floor your dance floor.For young visitors and families:Playdates (Every Saturday, from January 2027) – co-produced with leading immersive theatre company Punchdrunk Enrichment. A new experience for families will bring magic to the museum’s galleries, in pursuit of one of London’s most elusive creatures. Recommended for ages 7+.Showspace (Sundays from November 2026, Sunday to Friday from February 2027) – Sensory storytelling and performance bring to life events of the Great Fire, Roman London and other hidden stories that have shaped our city in these free interactive shows for schools and families. Recommended for ages 5+.

The museum will invite Guest Editors to explore the city through their eyes, reflecting on one of four key themes: tastes, sounds, plays and wears. Their ideas will act as a unifying thread, shaping a season of experiences and events that run through Our Time, including its regular house parties, family events and dinner clubs, as well as influencing the museum’s shop and restaurant. In a vibrant, evolving city of almost 10 million people, they will offer visitors the chance to experience a slice of their city. The museum’s inaugural programme, London Tastes (November 2026 – August 2027) will celebrate the city’s rich and vibrant food culture, led by Guest Editors Ruby Tandoh (All Consuming, Cook As You Are), whose work explores the intersections of food and social change, and Jonathan Nunn, founder of the influential food publication Vittles. The programme is sponsored by Sainsbury’s, whose roots in London date back to its first store on Drury Lane over 150 years ago.London Tastes will feature a spotlight exhibition across two display pavilions, exploring the changing appetites of a global food city. Crossing London’s neighbourhoods from Enfield to Park Royal, Southall to Walworth, it will touch on stories of Covent Garden market, Brick Lane, London’s traditional pie and mash shops, chicken shop culture, and the markets, manufacturers, retailers and artisans that make up London’s ever-evolving food scene.Mark Given, Chief Technology, Marketing and Data Officer at Sainsbury's said: "Good food has always been about bringing people together across communities, cultures and generations and for more than 150 years, Sainsbury's has been part of that story. From our first store at 173 Drury Lane, helping Londoners shop, cook and gather has always been at the heart of what we do.We're thrilled to come on board as Principal Sponsor of London Tastes – the debut creative programme at the brand-new London Museum – a programme that celebrates the rich heritage and food culture of this city, while looking ahead to the future. This partnership is a brilliant reflection of what we stand for at Sainsbury’s too – championing good food for all of us.”
A visualisation of London Museum’s Past Time galleries © Secchi Smith Atelier Brückner.

Descending below ground into the permanent galleries set at Roman street level, visitors will encounter the stories and people that have shaped London through time – from the lives of the earliest prehistoric inhabitants and rare artefacts from the city’s Roman origins nearly 2000 years ago, to transformative events including the Great Fire and the Blitz, and cultural milestones like the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Voices of past Londoner’s will shine through in object-rich, theatrical and sensory displays, presented both chronologically and thematically for the first time.Drawn from the museum’s 7-million-strong collection – the world’s largest relating to a single urban centre – Past Time reveals a city shaped as much by its grit as its glitter. In its first permanent display, the Cheapside Hoard will dazzle alongside rare objects from the Goldsmiths’ Company collection. Old favourites will return including the glamorous Selfridges lift and a chunk of the infamous Whitechapel Fatberg. There will be artefacts linked to iconic Londoners and defining moments for the capital – including Tom Daley’s 2012 Olympic diving trunks, Queen Victoria’s mourning dress, Charles Dickens’ chair and the vest believed to have been worn by King Charles I at his execution (on display for six months).London’s rich history as an epicentre of protest and activism is also explored, from an unparalleled collection of suffragette material – including Emmeline Pankhurst’s hunger strike medal and the court warrant issued to Sophia Duleep Singh – to more contemporary objects such as a statuette of Lady Phyll, co-founder of UK Black Pride, and placards from trailblazing disabled-led group Transport for All. From punk to ballet, London’s status as a global creative powerhouse will shine through iconic cultural artefacts: On loan from The Clash’s Paul Simonon, the smashed Fender Precision Bass guitar, immortalised on the band’s 1979 album London Calling, tablas belonging to British Bhangra pioneer Kuljit Bhamra and Anna Pavlova’s Dying Swan costume.Set amongst displays exploring London's evolving landscape, a six-metre viewing window will offer visitors a world first museum experience: the chance to watch live trains rumble through the galleries as passengers peer in from the passing Thameslink line.
A visualisation of London Museum’s train window in the Past Time galleries © Secchi Smith Atelier Brückner.
The restored General Market dome © London Museum.

Opened in 1883 and designed by Sir Horace Jones – the architect behind Tower Bridge and Leadenhall Market – the Victorian General Market saw over a century of trade before being shuttered in the 1990s and falling into disrepair. Leading its meticulous restoration and transformation are Stanton Williams and Asif Khan, working with conservation architects Julian Harrap. Together they are moulding a historic landmark into a sustainable 21st century cultural destination.The vast project has drawn on expertise from over 70 trades, and since 2023 has given more than 40 apprentices a start in fields ranging from plumbing and electrical engineering to emerging disciplines like sustainable construction management. The building’s heritage as a working market is being carefully preserved and celebrated through the work of some of the UK’s leading craftspeople – from the country’s last heritage coppersmiths to master stonemasons and Welsh blacksmiths restoring decorative ironwork. The reanimation of these historic buildings has been guided by their distinctive character – with features including a rediscovered 800sqm system of vaults beneath London’s streets and a perimeter of heritage shopfronts. At the same time, the project will be futureproofed for generations to come as a world-leading ‘green museum’. Incorporating cutting-edge sustainability measures – from toilets powered by rainwater to renewable geothermal energy and an industry-first eco-concrete mix – it is set to rank among the top 1% of buildings worldwide with a BREEAM ‘Outstanding’ sustainability rating.In the district of Smithfield, the museum will be embedded in an area that has been a centre for trade and exchange for almost a millennium, opposite the 900-year-old St Bartholomew’s Hospital with its elegant Hogarth Staircase, and a stone’s throw away from the internationally renowned Barbican Arts Centre and London’s majestic icon: St Paul’s Cathedral. The surrounding City of London is the capital’s most historic quarter, a former home to Shakespeare and depicted in the books of Charles Dickens, it has provided the backdrop to numerous films, TV series and music videos ranging from The Crown to Slow Horses, thanks to its iconic mix of architecture. It is home to an extraordinary 600 listed buildings, 28 conservation areas, 48 scheduled ancient monuments and four historic parks and gardens.ENDS

London Museum is London’s shared place in the middle of it all.No matter where you’ve come from, how long you’re staying for, or what side of the river you live on, we offer a home for exploration and adventure where all of London’s stories cross and collide.At our heart we're a social history museum and we tell the stories of how London came to be. But we're also contemporary collectors keeping our finger on the pulse. We're the world's biggest city museum.At the core of London Museum is our collection, which covers 450,000 years of history through seven million objects drawn from across all 33 boroughs. It's the largest collection in the world relating to a single urban centre.

The City of London Corporation is one of the largest funders of heritage and cultural activities in the UK, investing over £145m every year. It manages a range of world-class cultural and heritage institutions, including the Barbican Centre, Tower Bridge, Guildhall School of Music & Drama, Guildhall Library, Guildhall Art Gallery and London’s Roman Amphitheatre, The London Archives, and Keats House. It also supports the London Symphony Orchestra, based at the Barbican Centre, and the new London Museum.

items.title: GTA 6 breaks launch records
items.note: Now it's out: an estimated $2.36bn and 24.5M+ units on day one, per Sensor Tower.
items.read: Grand Theft Auto 6 launched Thursday after a 13-year wait and is estimated to be the biggest entertainment launch in history. Sensor Tower puts pre-orders plus first-day sales above 24.5 million units, about three quarters on PS5. Rockstar and Take-Two haven't released figures but call demand "unprecedented".

article.html:
4 hours ago

Osmond ChiaBusiness reporter

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have become the biggest entertainment launch in history following the blockbuster video game's debut on Thursday, after a 13-year wait.

The highly anticipated open-world action-adventure saw pre-orders and first day sales total more than 24.5 million units, raking in about $2.36bn (£1.8bn), according to analytics platform Sensor Tower.

GTA 6's maker Rockstar and parent company Take-Two have not released details of the game's sales but said demand has been "unprecedented". The BBC has contacted both the firms for comment.

At its core, the series is a satirical take on the American dream, putting players in the shoes of career criminals in Leonida, the game's Florida-inspired state.

The latest release follows new characters Lucia and her partner Jason, a pair of small-time criminals.

Sensor Tower said GTA 6 will be so popular that it will reduce the time gamers spend on other single-player titles by 10%.

The research firm said its estimates are based on email receipts data and other statistical sources that track millions of people daily. They also track public profiles across major gaming platforms like PlayStation and Xbox, where GTA 6 is available.

Around three quarters of the game's sales have been for the PlayStation 5 and the balance on Xbox, Sensor Tower said.

Niko Partners, a gaming market research firm, said it expects GTA 6 to make more than $3bn in sales worldwide this year.

That figure would rank GTA 6 among the highest-grossing entertainment releases ever, but it would still have some way to go to catch 1939's Gone with the Wind, which has made an estimated $4.5bn, adjusted for inflation.

Rockstar is expected to make even more money from GTA 6 over the coming years.

The New York-based studio has yet to announce when the game will be released for PCs or given a date for its multiplayer expansion, which will allow players to interact and go on missions with others over the internet.

If 2013's GTA 5 is any guide, multiplayer will add dozens more hours of gameplay and bring in even more revenue for Rockstar as players spend real money on in-game property, cars and other perks.

GTA 6 has been hailed by some reviewers as one of the most impressive gaming experiences ever. Entertainment media site IGN described it as an "uncompromisingly engineered" masterpiece.

The release of GTA 6 at midnight on Thursday across various time zones saw many gamers stay up through the night, while some took the following day off to play.

Its launch broke Virgin Media O2's evening traffic record as people rushed to install GTA 6's huge 212GB file on consoles.

The game's graphic content has resulted in censorship in Japan and, like earlier GTA releases, is not approved for sale in mainland China.

items.title: Huawei Nova 16s & 16s Pro
items.note: Out today in Malaysia: 200MP camera on the Pro, 7,000mAh battery and 100W charging.
items.read: Huawei's new mid-range Nova 16s series has 5G Kirin chips, 7,000mAh batteries and 100W fast charging. The Nova 16s Pro has a 200MP main camera with a 1/1.28-inch sensor, and both models have a 50MP periscope telephoto.

article.html:
Huawei has officially launched its latest Nova 16s series in Malaysia which comes in two models: Nova 16s and Nova 16s Pro. The new mid-range smartphones offer 5G connectivity powered by Huawei’s Kirin processors, large 7,000mAh batteries and 100W fast charging.

The main highlight is the higher-end Nova 16s Pro, which features a 200MP main camera with a large 1/1.28-inch sensor. Both models also come with a dedicated 50MP periscope telephoto camera for optical zoom.

The Huawei Nova 16s series is now available and Huawei Malaysia is offering launch rebates of up to RM600.

Huawei Nova 16s and 16s Pro Malaysia Pricing and Availability

The Huawei Nova 16s series is officially priced in Malaysia as follows:

  • Huawei Nova 16s 12GB+256GB – RM2,599 (RM1,999 after RM600 rebate)
  • Huawei Nova 16s Pro 12GB+512GB – RM3,299 (RM2,899 after RM400 rebate)

For the launch promotion, Huawei is offering free gifts and services worth up to RM1,956. This includes a Huawei Band 11 worth RM189, a Huawei 100W charger worth RM119 and one year of screen protector replacements worth RM49.

In addition, customers will receive Huawei premium services valued at up to RM1,599, comprising a one-year Worry-Free Care Package and a one-year APAC & MEA warranty.

In terms of colour options, the Nova 16s Pro comes in Breathing Crystal and Starry Black, while the standard Nova 16s is available in Breathing Crystal, Sky White and Starry Black.

Both devices are available through the Huawei Malaysia online store, as well as Huawei’s official stores on Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop.

The Huawei Nova 16s Pro is the higher-end model of the two, featuring a 6.84-inch OLED display with a resolution of 2856×1320 pixels. The screen supports a 1-120Hz LTPO adaptive refresh rate, 2160Hz PWM dimming and a claimed peak brightness of up to 6,000 nits.

Under the hood, the Nova 16s Pro runs on Huawei’s Kirin 9010S octa-core processor, paired with 512GB of internal storage. It also supports 5G connectivity.

For photography, the Nova 16s Pro gets a 200MP RYYB main camera with a large 1/1.28-inch sensor, an f/1.8 aperture and optical image stabilisation (OIS). This is accompanied by a 50MP RYYB periscope telephoto camera offering 3.7x optical zoom with OIS, and a 50MP RYYB ultra-wide-angle camera with a 118-degree field of view and support for macro photography at distances as close as 2.5cm.

There’s also a dedicated 1.5MP True-to-Colour multispectral camera designed to improve colour accuracy, particularly when capturing skin tones.

Up front, the Nova 16s Pro gets a 50MP selfie camera with a 1/2.5-inch sensor, accompanied by another True-to-Colour sensor. Huawei also offers 0.8x to 5x selfie and group selfie zoom, allowing users to adjust their framing for individual portraits and group shots.

In terms of battery, the Nova 16s Pro packs a large 7,000mAh battery, up from 5,500mAh on its predecessor. It supports 100W Huawei SuperCharge Turbo wired charging, which Huawei claims can deliver up to 40% charge in 15 minutes.

Despite the large battery, the device measures just 7.1mm thick and weighs approximately 218g. It also features an aluminium alloy frame, Kunlun Glass protection, WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 and NFC.

Out of the box, the Nova 16s Pro runs on EMUI 16. Huawei has also included several AI-powered photography features, including AI Composition for framing suggestions, AI Move for repositioning objects, AI Remove for removing unwanted subjects, AI De-glare for reducing reflections and AI Best Expression for improving group photos.

The device also supports cross-platform file transfers with compatible Apple devices through the Petal Interconnect app.

Huawei Nova 16s specs and features

The standard Huawei Nova 16s offers a slightly smaller 6.68-inch OLED display with a resolution of 2800×1280 pixels. It supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz, 2160Hz PWM dimming and a claimed peak brightness of up to 5,500 nits.

Instead of the Kirin 9010S, the regular Nova 16s runs on Huawei’s Kirin 8020 octa-core processor, paired with 256GB of internal storage. It also supports 5G connectivity.

For photography, the Nova 16s gets a 50MP main camera with an f/1.9 aperture, accompanied by a 50MP RYYB periscope telephoto camera offering 3.3x optical zoom and OIS. There’s also a dedicated 1.5MP True-to-Colour multispectral sensor designed to improve colour accuracy.

Unlike the Pro, the standard Nova 16s misses out on an ultra-wide-angle camera and optical image stabilisation for its main 50MP camera.

Up front, you still get a 50MP selfie camera, but without the additional True-to-Colour sensor found on the Pro model.

Similar to the Pro, the standard Nova 16s gets a 7,000mAh battery with support for 100W Huawei SuperCharge Turbo wired charging. The device is slightly lighter at approximately 199g, although it is marginally thicker at 7.3mm.

It also supports WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 and NFC, and runs on EMUI 16 out of the box.

Both Nova 16s smartphones offer the same AI-powered photography and editing features, as well as cross-platform file sharing through Petal Interconnect. As usual, Huawei smartphones do not come with Google Mobile Services pre-installed, and users will have to rely on Huawei AppGallery and other supported methods to access their preferred apps.

items.title: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage
items.note: A world first: Mechazilla's 'chopsticks' caught Ship 42 back at Starbase.
items.read: On Starship's 15th test flight, SpaceX caught the upper stage, Ship 42, with the launch tower's arms for the first time, about 22.5 hours after liftoff. The Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf splashdown after a low-fuel alarm, so a full-vehicle catch didn't happen. SpaceX called it "the holy grail of spaceflight".

items.title: Kutra (كترة)
items.note: An Asir-inspired specialty cafe in An Nuzhah, praised for clear V60s and a well-textured Madrid cheesecake.
items.read: Arab News (6 Nov 2026) says Kutra began in Al-Namas and now runs a two-floor cafe and roastery in Riyadh, with Asiri-inspired interiors and a traditional nijr. The reviewer liked the Ethiopian Guji and especially the Brazilian Catuai V60s, called the house-roast flat white beautifully balanced, and said the Madrid cheesecake nails the texture. Outdoor tables look out on Uthman Ibn Affan Road. An Exa place listing puts it in An Nuzhah, at 4.7 from 334 reviews, open daily 6:30 a.m. to 1 a.m.
facts: Uthman Ibn Affan Rd, Abi Sfyan Ibn Harb, An Nuzhah 12474

article.html:
RIYADH: Kutra brings a distinctive southern character to Riyadh, combining specialty coffee, traditional design and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

Originally established in Al-Namas, in southern Saudi Arabia, Kutra operates as both a cafe and a roastery, offering high-quality, internationally sourced coffee beans roasted locally in Asir.

This connection to its origins is reflected throughout the space with the elegant Asiri-inspired interiors and the traditional nijr, a mortar and pestle whose rhythmic sound was once associated with hospitality and welcoming guests.

The cafe is spacious, spread across two floors, yet maintains a cozy, intimate atmosphere. Natural sunlight fills the interior through large tinted windows, allowing visitors to enjoy the brightness without the harsh glare.

The second floor offers additional seating and a private meeting room, making it suitable for community gatherings, informal work sessions or more important meetings.

The outdoor seating is particularly charming, with uneven-shaped wooden tables that complement the cafe’s natural aesthetic. Overlooking Othman bin Affan Road, the outdoor area offers a relaxed setting that I imagine will be especially lovely during Riyadh’s upcoming cool winter months.

Coffee is undoubtedly one of Kutra’s strongest offerings. I tried two V60 selections: the Ethiopian Guji, which was lovely, and the Brazilian Catuai, which was particularly impressive and easily worth returning for.

I also ordered a flat white made with their classic house roast, which was beautifully balanced and especially enjoyable.

The cafe offers lactose-free and low-fat milk, but no non-dairy alternatives. I also tried their matcha, which was fairly unremarkable.

Their Madrid cheesecake, however, was another highlight. I have tried this dessert at several cafes, and few get the consistency right, but Kutra nails the texture. The menu also includes a variety of hot and cold beverages alongside signature desserts.

Beyond the food and drinks, Kutra stands out for its sense of identity. The Asiri-inspired details feel thoughtfully incorporated rather than simply decorative, while the spacious layout, comfortable seating and abundance of natural light make it an inviting place to spend time. The cafe also offers souvenirs for visitors who want to take home a small reminder of the experience.

Service was attentive, prices were average, and the overall atmosphere was calm and family-friendly.

items.title: Crops
items.note: A neighborhood specialty roastery in Al Narjis that opens at 6 a.m., with a much-praised chocolate-chip banana bread.
items.read: Arab News (24 Sep 2026) describes Crops as a cozy specialty roastery in a residential corner of Al-Narjis, open 6 a.m. to midnight. The reviewer recommended pairing a creamy flat white with the chocolate-chip banana bread, and noted quiet work seating, no background music, and eight bean varieties (Ethiopia, Colombia, El Salvador, Peru and Brazil) also sold wholesale. An Exa listing at السهام, An Narjis, rates it 4.4 from 1,517 reviews. Evenings and after Friday prayers are the busy times, and parking can be tight then.
facts: Flat white, banana bread, in-house roasting

article.html:
A careful balance of traditional warmth and modern sophistication defines Crops, a neighborhood specialty roastery in Al-Narjis, Riyadh.

On a recent visit, the flat white was rich, smooth and creamy, with talented barista latte art on top; and the banana bread, one of the best in Riyadh, with chocolate chips, was well flavored and balanced. Together, they made a satisfying and recommended pairing.

The interior carries the same sense of balance. A traditional carpet adds warmth and cultural character, while the wide-wall abstract painting, soft lighting, wooden furniture, and leather seating give the cafe a contemporary finish.

Seating options range from a common workstation with convenient power sockets to cosy sofas, making the space suitable for working alone or socializing. The absence of background music makes it easier to focus too.

Open from 6 a.m. to midnight, the cafe accommodates students and workers looking for a quiet coffee before business hours. It is particularly busy in the evenings and after Friday prayers, as neighbors head there to enjoy coffee with family and friends on the weekend.

Its location in a residential neighborhood, away from busy main roads, adds to its cosy character. The setting is calm and convenient during off-peak hours, though finding parking in the evening is unsurprisingly a challenge.

The cafe is known for its high-quality roasting and offers eight varieties of coffee beans, available for wholesale purchase through its website.

For aficionados who enjoy exploring origins and flavor profiles, the selection includes single-origin and blended beans sourced from Ethiopia, Colombia, El Salvador, Peru and Brazil.

The range moves from fruity, floral notes to richer chocolate, caramel, and nutty profiles, with beans suited to drip coffee, espresso, and milk-based drinks.

With quality coffee, flexible hours and an effortlessly welcoming atmosphere, the roastery serves several purposes while retaining the intimacy of a neighborhood cafe, calling you to visit repeatedly.

items.read: Fiestahan Asian & Pinoy Cuisine has served Riyadh's Filipino community since 2018 from inside Al Jazeera Supermarket (Aswaaq Al Jazeera) on Musa Bin Naseer Street in Al Sulaymaniyah / Al Olaya. The restaurant's site highlights Iniwow sa Bilao, Chicken BBQ on stick and Bacolod Cansi, and notes a live band from about 7:30 p.m. Thursday to Saturday. It is open daily 11:30 a.m.–11:45 p.m., with free parking and a family section. An Exa listing rates the Sulaymaniyah branch 4.5 from 1,301 reviews.

items.title: StepGrab
items.note: Turns every click into a numbered, annotated how-to guide, and keeps the screenshots on your computer.
items.read: StepGrab is a menu-bar app for macOS 14+ and Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 that screenshots each click, adds numbered arrows, and builds a step-by-step guide. The site says capture works offline and screenshots stay on your computer, with no account and no upload. A free plan covers unlimited guides of up to 15 steps and, on the Mac, every export format (GIF, PDF, MP4, HTML, Markdown and mobile video) with a small “Made with stepgrab.net” mark; Windows 1.6 free export is GIF only. The developer’s October 2026 pricing page lists StepGrab Pro at $12.99 a year, or $44.99 for a lifetime license, which removes the mark and can add your logo.

Mac · Windows

New in 1.7 for Mac: every export format is free

The automatic step-by-step guide creator.

StepGrab takes a screenshot at every click, adds numbered arrows, and builds the guide for you, on Mac and Windows. Use it for Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), tutorials and onboarding. Capture works offline, and your screenshots stay on your computer.

Also in the Mac App Store · Microsoft Store

Features

Everything you need. Nothing you don't.

Auto Capture

Start recording and click through your workflow. Every click becomes one step, with the screenshot taken at the moment you click.

Looks hand-crafted

Record one window and every step shows just that window with rounded corners and shadow, no desktop behind it. On Mac, when you record a whole display, StepGrab hides desktop icons and widgets, and the menu bar if you want.

Menus & dropdowns included

When you record a window, its open menus, pop-up menus, popovers and sheets stay in the step picture. Each click step can use the picture from just before you clicked: always on Windows, on Mac with Capture the frame before the click in Settings.

Smart Annotations

Numbered arrows land precisely where you clicked, in your color, size, and style, so your audience always knows where to look.

Export in any format

Export your workflow as GIF, PDF, MP4, HTML, Markdown or mobile video, free on the Mac with a small “Made with stepgrab.net” mark, ready to share in seconds.

Lives in your menu bar

Always one click away, with a lightweight floating HUD that shows your step count and live previews while you record.

New in StepGrab 1.7 for Mac

Almost everything is free now.

  • Every export format, free. GIF, PDF, MP4, HTML, Markdown and mobile video, each with a small “Made with stepgrab.net” mark. Pro removes the mark and adds your own logo.
  • Redact automatically. Turn it on and StepGrab blacks out emails, phone numbers, addresses, credentials and payment data while you record, or afterward for one step or all. Detection does not find everything, so check your steps before you share them.
  • Continue from here, recapture a step. Add new steps after any step, or redo a single click without recording the whole guide again.
  • Four styles, all free. Standard, Fine, Curved and Focus for the arrow and badge, with Customize for arrow, badge, effects and cursor. If an arrow stands out too little, contrast assist adds an outline.

StepGrab for Windows is still on version 1.6, where the free plan exports GIF. Version 1.7 for Windows is coming soon.

How it works

Four steps. One guide.

Perfect for Employee Onboarding Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) Customer Support Tutorials Software Documentation Bug Reporting Training Manuals See examples →

Your screen never leaves your computer.

Captured on your computer.
Screenshots never uploaded.

Offline Capture

Recording needs no internet connection. Recordings, screenshots, and exports stay on your computer. StepGrab never uploads them.

No StepGrab Account

No StepGrab account: no sign-up, no password.

No Cloud Upload

Your screen never leaves your device. You decide what gets shared, and with whom.

One file, shared safely

A project is now a single file that also opens in StepGrab for Windows. Projects from earlier versions still open. A project still contains the original, unredacted screenshots, and StepGrab warns you about that. To share it, turn on Burn in redactions in File › Save As: the copy has the boxes burned into the images and no originals, so the recipient cannot undo the redaction. Your project keeps the originals.

App Store purchases run through Apple's StoreKit. The app itself has no third-party analytics and no ad SDKs.

I've been using StepGrab for a short time, and it does exactly what it promises. It automatically captures screenshots while you work through a process, making it much easier to create step-by-step guides without stopping to take screenshots manually. The interface is simple and easy to understand, and the generated guides save a lot of time when documenting workflows. It's especially useful for creating SOPs, training materials, or tutorials. Overall, it's a practical tool that helps streamline documentation with minimal effort.

User guides made fast

StepGrab is ideal for quickly creating tutorials for users. Working with the editor is a bit unusual at times, but what's really great: the developer responds quickly and is open to suggestions.
In short: great app, and I'm excited to see how the app continues to develop over time!

gkoederApp Store · Germany

The preview and editing features in 1.4.0 make this a real timesaver

This will now save me quite a bit of time compared with Screenshot.app paired with Preview or another annotation tool; the preview and editing/reordering features make this a genuinely useful tool for those who need to share computer task instructions.

tinyappsApp Store · United States

Great app, but the free plan is too limited

Thanks for creating such a helpful app! StepGrab has already saved me a lot of time and made my workflow much easier.
However, I have to say that the free version feels quite limited in terms of functionality. I reached the usage limit very quickly and now need to upgrade to continue using the app properly.
Apart from that, it’s a great app with a lot of potential. I really like the concept and the overall experience — I just hope the free tier could offer a bit more functionality for users who are still trying it out.

ClaraM04App Store · Italy

Unfortunately, it's too expensive for individuals

That's nice, but 50 euros is still too expensive for individual consumers. It would be great if R… also gave out coupons for the App Store.

Egg Bear MusicianApp Store · Germany

Works well for me

So far it’s working well for me. I just need to make easy to follow, step by step instructions for non-technical staff members who need to perform specific operations on our community web site.

I had grown weary of manually taking screen shots and trying to assemble something usable when I saw the announcement for this on Reddit. I bought the Pro license. I have some suggestions that I will submit to the developer.

nonicknamebecausenoneavailableApp Store · United States

What's great: it lives quietly in the menu bar and just works when i need it. i record a task once and get back a clean set of annotated screenshots with the click arrows already drawn on, which used to be the most tedious part of writing internal docs for me. the fact that nothing leaves the machine matters too, since some of what i document has account settings and pricing info i wouldn't want uploaded anywhere.

What needs improvement: the step descriptions get vague on toolbar icons that don't have visible text - it reads the label fine when there is one, but an unlabeled icon button just gets described generically. would love better handling there as the underlying model improves.

vs Alternatives: looked at scribe briefly but it's web-first and subscription only, and i didn't want screen recordings of internal tools sitting on someone else's server.

Promising, but the free tier left me with nothing usable…

I was really excited to try StepGrab and put a good amount of time into building out an SOP. When I went to download it, I thought something was broken: the only export option was a GIF. That's when I realized the free tier is much more limited than I expected.

If the free tier is going to be this restricted, please make the export limits clear up front, before people invest time building something. Honestly, I would have preferred no downloads at all on the free tier. That would have pushed me to fully weigh the payment decision before I sank so much time into an SOP I can't use.

gate.keeper268App Store · United States

Did not work for me, they really mean “Zero Editing”

I guess I should not have been surprised but it was when I found there is very little control over what the app creates other than size of some of the elements. But if it decides to place the step badges over critical text, you have zero control. Nor can you annotate to add clarifying information critical in many scenarios. I think its over priced for what little it does at this point.

Update 9/15/26: The latest update 1.40 now adds a fair amount of control over placement that wasn’t there previously. There are still some gotchas that make this useful in many scenarios but not all. You may need other screen capture tools if creating complex graphics or if you want to compress several steps onto one screen cap. Overall it’s worth a try, but still a bit pricey for what is offered. On the plus side the developer is actively engaged and responds to feedback.

Formats

Export in any format.

Video

MP4

A 16:9 video of all steps. Each step stays on screen for 0.5 to 5 seconds with its arrow and step number, plus optional captions and a click ripple. Add it to a doc or your video platform.

Animated

GIF

Looping preview clip for product updates, Slack threads, and GitHub pull requests. Free on Mac and Windows, with a small StepGrab mark.

Document

PDF

Numbered, printable step-by-step guide with one page per step. Step text and screenshots included.

Web page

HTML

A web page that opens in any browser, offline and without StepGrab. Readers page through one step at a time, zoom into the click, link to a single step or print all steps. Send it as one file or as a folder.

Text

Markdown

A .md file with a heading, sentence and image link for each step, plus a folder of images next to it. Ready for GitHub, Notion, Obsidian and wikis.

Social

Mobile

A video for TikTok, Reels and Shorts in 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5. Each step sits on a drawn MacBook or monitor with the step text below. Add one PNG per step for slideshows.

Step editor

A dedicated step editor.

Fix every step before you export.

Check and fix every step inside StepGrab, before you export.

  • Grab the arrows. Drag the number for direction and length, drag the middle to bend the curve, or flip the elbow to the other side.
  • Rewrite and format the sentences. Click a step description and write your own, with bold, italic, underline, text color, highlight, lists and alignment. Clear it and the suggestion comes back. Your text shows up in exports .
  • Redact and mark. Drag a box over names or customer data and it turns solid black in every export. StepGrab’s suggested sentence for that step then leaves out the element’s name; sentences you wrote stay as they are. Draw a rectangle, ellipse or circle to point at a spot without hiding it. Or let StepGrab find them: auto redact covers emails, phone numbers, addresses, credentials and payment data, for one step or all.
  • A preview per format. GIF, PDF , HTML  and Mobile  each show what the export will contain.
  • Reorder and undo. Sort by drag and drop, delete what you don’t need, take it back with ⌘Z.

A closer look

Small app. Full control.

The floating HUD keeps you in flow.

While you record, a lightweight panel shows your status, step count, and live thumbnails of every capture. Drop a step you don't need, undo the last one, continue, or export without ever leaving your workflow.

Your guides, your look.

Pick one of four styles (Standard, Fine, Curved or Focus) and fine-tune the arrow, the number badge, the numbering (1, 01, A or none), effects and the cursor under Customize. Set one brand color for arrows and accents; if an arrow stands out too little, contrast assist adds an outline. All of this is free. Show the cursor at the click point and hide desktop icons. Add brand profiles Pro and your own logo Pro so every export looks like yours.

Set up once. It just works.

Light or dark exports, Dock icon on or off, launch at login, HUD position and previews: StepGrab adapts to the way you work, then stays out of your way.

Keyboard shortcuts as steps

Shortcuts such as ⌘S, plus Return, Tab, Escape and the arrow keys, become their own steps with key caps in the picture once you allow the optional Input Monitoring permission on your Mac.

Double-clicks and scrolling

A double-click is recorded as one step instead of two, and scrolling before a click is noted in the next step’s sentence.

Save it, finish it later

Save a guide as a .stepgrab project with ⌘S, reopen it from Open Recent and press Continue to add steps (on the free plan, the 15 steps include the ones already in the project). Since version 1.6, a project is a single file that also opens in StepGrab for Windows.

Siri and Shortcuts

Start a new recording, stop it or export the guide with Siri or a tile in the Shortcuts app, and use all five StepGrab actions in your own shortcuts and automations.

Seven languages on Mac and Windows

The Mac app works in English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese, and you can set the guide language Pro for each guide, separate from the app language. StepGrab for Windows has the same seven languages.

AI text (on-device) Pro

With macOS 26 and Apple Intelligence turned on, Apple’s on-device model rewords the suggested sentences when you export, without changing names, positions or click types.

items.note: A free Mac app that names the devices on your Wi-Fi in plain English and flags risky open ports on the LAN.
items.read: Netfox is a native macOS network monitor that turns raw device names into plain English and checks machines on your LAN for commonly exposed ports such as remote access, file sharing and forgotten dev servers. The site says it uses no cloud and no account, stays on your Mac, and will not probe anything outside your network. When the page was opened on 20 Nov 2026 it listed version 0.55.0, support for macOS 15.6+ on Apple Silicon and Intel, 77 releases since May 2026, and 2,880 downloads. It is free, signed and notarized.
